diagram_math_checks.result: Top internal row is (0,0,0); middle and bottom internal rows are (Z/2,Z/4,Z/2), with zero endpoint groups. i:Z/2→Z/4 sends [x]₂ to [2x]₄; changing x by 2 changes 2x by 4, so i is well-defined. q:Z/4→Z/2 sends [x]₄ to [x]₂; changing x by 4 changes its residue by 0 modulo 2. Both preserve addition. The three upper vertical maps are 0→G; the three lower maps are 1_G:G→G. All 12 horizontal and 6 vertical arrows have the domains/codomains specified in Example lines 34–42 and Verification 1.1.

Upper-left internal square: i∘0=0∘(0→0)=0 as maps 0→Z/4. Upper-right internal square: q∘0=0∘(0→0)=0 as maps 0→Z/2. Lower-left internal square: 1_(Z/4)∘i=i∘1_(Z/2)=i. Lower-right internal square: 1_(Z/2)∘q=q∘1_(Z/4)=q. If zero-endpoint vertical arrows are filled in, their four boundary squares commute because every map to/from 0 composes to zero. This realizes exactly the commutative diagram described in the Example, with no sign choices.

Top row consists entirely of zero groups and is exact. In each other row, i has images [0]₄,[2]₄ and is injective; q hits [0]₂,[1]₂ and is surjective; ker q={[0]₄,[2]₄}=im i. Consequently 0→Z/2→Z/4→Z/2→0 is short exact at every group and endpoint, as Verification 1.1–2.1 states. Finite enumeration independently confirmed homomorphism laws, injectivity, surjectivity and image/kernel equality.
